header.name: Sun Pharmaceutical Industries Ltd
header.source: NSE closing price (end of day, not live); 52-week range computed from daily highs and lows (NSE bhavcopy)

claims.label: FACT
claims.text: Sun Pharmaceutical Industries (NSE: SUNPHARMA) makes and sells pharmaceuticals; its consolidated revenue in FY26 was ₹58,462 crore.

claims.label: CALCULATION
claims.text: In the quarter to 30 Sep 2026, revenue was ₹16,199 crore, 11.9% more than a year earlier; the operating margin was 24.6% against 26.2%, and profit attributable to shareholders was ₹1,989 crore, 36.2% lower.

claims.label: CALCULATION
claims.text: On 30 Oct 2026, the first session after the result, SUNPHARMA shares rose 0.95% while the NIFTY 50 rose 0.51% and the NIFTY PHARMA index rose 1.55%; allowing for the market's move, SUNPHARMA's own move was +0.68%, about 0.58 times its usual daily variation.

claims.label: UNCERTAIN
claims.text: These numbers measure the move, not its cause: the result, the pharma sector's rise and any other news that day overlap, and nothing here separates them.

claims.label: CALCULATION
claims.text: At ₹1,868 (NSE close, 16 Nov 2026), a discounted cash flow model with a 8.84% cost of capital matches the price if revenue grows about 14.0% a year for five years at the FY26 operating margin of 25.3%; SUNPHARMA's revenue grew 10.0% a year over FY23–FY26.

claims.label: CALCULATION
claims.text: With the other assumptions at base, the valuation is most sensitive to the cost of capital (one percentage point either way: a model value of ₹1,241 to ₹2,083 a share) and to how long SUNPHARMA keeps earning high returns on new investment (anywhere from returns equal to its cost of capital to a quarter above its past level: a model value of ₹1,075 to ₹1,613 a share); the Q3 FY27 result will be the next reported quarter.

prices.note: Each series is rebased to 100 on the first common session. Raw exchange prices are not published here (NSE terms).

metrics.label: Market cap
metrics.definition: Price × shares outstanding (share capital ÷ ₹1 face value at 2026-09-30).

metrics.label: P/E (TTM)
metrics.definition: Price ÷ earnings per share over the last four reported quarters (Q3 FY26 – Q2 FY27).

metrics.label: EV / EBIT (TTM)
metrics.definition: Enterprise value (market cap − the net cash and treasury figure below) ÷ operating profit over the last four quarters.

metrics.label: Net cash and treasury
metrics.definition: Cash, bank balances and treasury investments, less lease liabilities, borrowings, preference shares and minority interests, at 30 Sep 2026.

metrics.label: Operating margin (FY26)
metrics.definition: EBIT ÷ revenue, after depreciation, excluding other income. Sites that quote an EBITDA-based margin show a higher figure.

metrics.label: ROE (FY26)
metrics.definition: Profit for the year ÷ total equity at year end.

metrics.label: ROIC (FY26)
metrics.definition: After-tax EBIT ÷ invested capital at the start of the year. Invested capital excludes about ₹29k crore of cash and treasury, which is why it looks so high.

metrics.label: Revenue growth FY23–FY26
metrics.definition: Compound annual growth of revenue from FY23 to FY26.

metrics.label: Cash conversion (FY26)
metrics.definition: Operating cash flow ÷ profit for the year.

metrics.label: Beta vs NIFTY 50
metrics.definition: Sensitivity of SUNPHARMA's daily return to the NIFTY 50's, over the two years to the price date.

scenarios.name: Bear
scenarios.what: Revenue grows only at FY26's pace for five years, the operating margin slips 2 points, and growth after year 10 earns no more than its cost of capital.

scenarios.name: Base
scenarios.what: Revenue keeps its FY23-FY26 growth rate for five years, the FY26 margin holds, and SUNPHARMA keeps its historical return on capital indefinitely.

scenarios.name: Bull
scenarios.what: Revenue grows at H1 FY27's year-on-year pace for five years and the margin rises 1 point.

valuation.rule_note: The cost of debt and long-run growth are set by fixed rules and not reviewed by a person.

limitations: Template A (non-financial, positive free cash flow). Single-stage fade model; no currency driver.
Cash flows are discounted to the balance-sheet date, 30 Sep 2026, two months before the price date; the model does not roll that gap forward, so its values are slightly low against the price.
Debt is borrowings plus lease liabilities; earmarked bank balances are counted as cash, which overstates cash slightly.
The risk-free rate is a twelve-month average while the price and equity risk premium are point-in-time.
The event study measures the size of a move, not its cause; five results days are too few for statistical claims.
Sun Pharma's results are printed in INR million; the lease lines taken from its results PDFs are converted to INR crore by the engine, and each says so.
From FY23 the figures come from the exchange XBRL filings; the lease liabilities for FY22 to FY25 come from the results PDFs (text layers checked against the printed subtotals and the XBRL).
Static page: prices are end-of-day as of the date shown, not live.
